title: Separate tables from rules
prompt: Write hit(hp,stats) using stats['damage'] and clamp at zero. Example: hp=45,damage=20 gives 25. Do not modify stats.
tests:
s={'damage':20}
assert hit(45,s)==25 and hit(10,s)==0, 'Apply damage with a zero-health floor'
assert hit(45,{'damage':5})==40, 'Read the parameter instead of hard-coding one card'
assert s=={'damage':20}, 'Do not alter the table row'

title: Audit a run manifest
prompt: Write comparable(a,b) returning True only if both contain engine,tables,adapter and those values match. Example: same engine but different tables is False.
tests:
a={'engine':'a','tables':'16.402.22','adapter':'v1'}
assert comparable(a,dict(a)), 'Identical complete manifests are comparable on these fields'
assert not comparable(a,{**a,'tables':'16.635.3'}), 'Different tables need explicit rebaselining'
assert not comparable({},{}), 'Two missing manifests are not evidence of equivalence'

title: Scale coordinates
prompt: Write to_engine(point) and to_pool(point), where point is a pair and engine scale is 18. Return tuples. Example: (1000,2000) maps to (18000,36000).
tests:
assert to_engine((1000,2000))==(18000,36000), 'Apply SCALE to both coordinates'
assert to_pool((81000,369000))==(4500,20500), 'Invert the documented scale'
assert to_pool(to_engine((3500,6500)))==(3500,6500), 'Round trip must preserve the point'
hint: A tuple comprehension can be built with tuple(generator).

title: Inspect the real adapter safely
prompt: Read pipeline/royale_env.py as text and assign scale, the integer literal on its SCALE assignment. Do not import the module. Example: a text line 'SCALE = 7 # comment' would yield 7.
starter:
from pathlib import Path
text=Path('pipeline/royale_env.py').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
# TODO: parse the line starting SCALE =
scale=0
solution:
from pathlib import Path
text=Path('pipeline/royale_env.py').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
scale=int(next(line.split('=',1)[1].split('#',1)[0].strip() for line in text.splitlines() if line.startswith('SCALE =')))
tests:
lines=Path('pipeline/royale_env.py').read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines()
expected=int(next(l.split('=',1)[1].split('#',1)[0].strip() for l in lines if l.startswith('SCALE =')))
assert isinstance(scale,int) and scale==expected and scale>0, 'Read the current positive integer SCALE without importing runtime code'
hint: split removes the assignment prefix and trailing comment.

title: Bound the conclusion
prompt: Write verdict(evidence): return 'exact' only if smoke,deterministic,all_frames_exact are all True; otherwise 'not established'. Missing fields fail. Example: smoke alone is not enough.
solution:
def verdict(evidence):
    return 'exact' if all(evidence.get(k) is True for k in ['smoke','deterministic','all_frames_exact']) else 'not established'
tests:
assert verdict({'smoke':True})=='not established', 'A smoke test does not prove exactness'
assert verdict({'smoke':True,'deterministic':True,'all_frames_exact':False})=='not established', 'Preserve a measured replay failure'
assert verdict({'smoke':True,'deterministic':True,'all_frames_exact':True})=='exact', 'All declared toy gates support the bounded verdict'
hint: Require explicit True for every field.
